items.label: list_item
items.text: 3Some solid potassium iodide was placed in an evaporating basin. Two carbon electrodes were inserted and connected to a 12 volt DC power source and a light bulb. The potassium iodide was heated. As soon as the potassium iodide was molten, the bulb came on. Purple fumes were seen coming from the positive electrode, and lilac flashes were seen around the negative one.

items.label: list_item
items.text: a Explain why the bulb didn't come on until the potassium iodide melted.

items.label: list_item
items.text: b State the name of the positive electrode.

items.label: list_item
items.text: c Name the purple fumes seen at the positive electrode, and write the ionic half-equation for their formation.

items.label: list_item
items.text: d The lilac flashes seen around the negative electrode are caused by the potassium which is formed. The potassium burns with a lilac flame. Write the ionic half-equation for the formation of the potassium.

items.label: list_item
items.text: e State the products formed at the electrodes if molten sodium bromide is electrolysed instead of molten potassium iodide.

items.label: list_item
items.text: fWrite the ionic half-equations for the reactions occurring during the electrolysis of molten sodium bromide.
